description: OpenClaw has a Trusted-proxy Control UI pairing bypass which allows unpaired node sessions
how_introduced: AI-assisted code in commit 20523b918adff4feae378ac9965e204c56b6e3d8 (co-authored by Cursor) directly introduced the vulnerable trusted-proxy pairing-bypass logic. That commit added a new `trustedProxyAuthOk` fast path for Control UI connections without preserving the existing operator-only role gate, which enabled unpaired node-role sessions.

bug_commits.author: SidQin-cyber
bug_commits.message: fix(gateway): allow trusted-proxy control-ui auth to skip device pairing

agent_verdicts.reasoning: The fix commit only adds `role === "operator"` to the new `trustedProxyAuthOk` condition in two places, and blame at the fix parent attributes those vulnerable lines to 20523b918. Pickaxe searches for `trustedProxyAuthOk`, `params.isControlUi && params.trustedProxyAuthOk`, and `resolvedAuth.mode === "trusted-proxy"` in this pairing-bypass context all identify 20523b918 as the first introduction. In that commit, `evaluateMissingDeviceIdentity()` gained `if (params.isControlUi && params.trustedProxyAuthOk) return { kind: "allow" }` and `shouldSkipControlUiPairing()` gained `if (trustedProxyAuthOk) return true`, while `message-handler.ts` computed `trustedProxyAuthOk` without any role check. Before this commit, the relevant logic only allowed bypass through `roleCanSkipDeviceIdentity(role, sharedAuthOk)`, which is explicitly operator-only; 20523b918 bypassed that restriction and made node-role Control UI sessions unpaired/authenticated under trusted-proxy mode.
